explanation: Greek poly, many, plus glotta, tongue. The same root gives glottis, the opening between the vocal cords, and glossary, a list of hard words.

claims.text: A polyglot is a person who knows and can use several languages.
A polyglot is not defined as someone who reads ancient scripts, writes with both hands or recites long poems.
Polyglot comes from Greek poly (many) and glotta (tongue, language).
Glottis and glossary come from the same Greek word for tongue (glotta, also glossa).
